generatedFrom.describes: governed white-label chrome emission table (written at :root per tenant)
authored DS stylesheets (root declarations = DS-owned foundation tokens)
DS component sources (var() reads = consumption without ownership)

derivation.publicHook: read by the DS via var() and owned by neither the tenant chrome channel nor a DS root declaration — or an owner-reviewed promotion, declared below
derivation.foundationToken: root-declared in authored DS CSS; the DS owns the value
derivation.tenantChannel: emitted at :root by the white-label chrome compiler on behalf of a tenant, including the families it builds by string interpolation

contract.mayAssign: a property listed in publicHooks, under an explicit application/feature scope
contract.mustNotAssign: anything in foundationTokens or tenantChannel, and nothing at all on a root or root-equivalent selector
contract.appNamespace: --rt-* is application-owned and always legal, including at root
contract.valueConstraint: an assignment to a promoted hook must chain through DS/tenant tokens; a raw colour literal would pin brand paint an application user cannot re-theme

--ds-command-grid-opacity.owner: the decorative command-grid overlay, `:where(.ds-command-grid)` in presentation/components/patterns.css
--ds-command-grid-opacity.slot: any application feature scope that contains a command-grid overlay
--ds-command-grid-opacity.fallback: 0.18 at the read site; 0.16 is the DS default declaration
--ds-command-grid-opacity.subtreeRepaint: one absolutely-positioned, pointer-events:none decorative element. No text, control or surface below the scope changes.
--ds-command-grid-opacity.rationale: The overlay exists to sit at different strengths on a hero, a matrix and a card; a single global opacity cannot serve all three. The chrome compiler emits the rest of the --ds-command-* family but deliberately not this one, so no tenant decision is at stake.

--ds-chart-plot-bg.slot: the chart panel element of an application chart surface
--ds-chart-plot-bg.valueType: <color> or <image> resolving through DS surface tokens
--ds-chart-plot-bg.subtreeRepaint: the plotting area of the chart that owns the scope; sibling charts and all surrounding chrome are untouched.
--ds-chart-plot-bg.rationale: Read with the documented component-variable fallback, which is the DS saying the panel may supply its own plot surface. Activity, heatmap and team charts each need a different plot ground within one page.

--ds-listing-grid-min-card-width.subtreeRepaint: grid track sizing inside the one collection that owns the scope. Geometry only — no colour, border or shadow is re-derived.
--ds-listing-grid-min-card-width.rationale: Density is a per-collection editorial decision: an applications board and an AI-interview board carry different card counts per row at the same brand. The tenant still owns every painted value of the grid.

--ds-listing-grid-gap.subtreeRepaint: grid track sizing inside the one collection that owns the scope. Geometry only — no colour, border or shadow is re-derived.
--ds-listing-grid-gap.rationale: Density is a per-collection editorial decision: an applications board and an AI-interview board carry different card counts per row at the same brand. The tenant still owns every painted value of the grid.

--ds-signal-card-accent.owner: the signal-card skin (premium card chrome family)
--ds-signal-card-accent.slot: an application card scope carrying a semantic tone attribute (data-signal-tone / data-metric-tone)
--ds-signal-card-accent.valueType: <color> resolving through DS semantic colour tokens
--ds-signal-card-accent.subtreeRepaint: the accent rule, soft wash and icon chip of the single card that owns the scope.
--ds-signal-card-accent.rationale: A signal card states success, warning or error. Those are semantic roles the tenant already owns as --ds-color-success/-warning/-error, and the tone attribute selects among them; the single compiled accent cannot express six tones at once. Every assignment chains to a tenant semantic colour.

--ds-metric-card-bg.owner: the metric-card structure (ui/structures/dashboard/insights) and premium card chrome
--ds-metric-card-bg.slot: an application metric-card scope under a declared anatomy axis (data-anatomy-card / data-anatomy-layout)
--ds-metric-card-bg.valueType: <length> for padding/min-height; DS shadow and surface tokens for bg/shadow
--ds-metric-card-bg.subtreeRepaint: metric cards inside the declared anatomy scope only.
--ds-metric-card-bg.rationale: The anatomy axis is a product-level layout mode (underline vs floating) that the DS exposes precisely so a vertical can restate card elevation and rhythm. The values re-express DS tokens — var(--ds-card-bg), var(--ds-shadow-none), var(--ds-spacing-4) — so the tenant palette continues to propagate.

--ds-tabs-list-bg.owner: the Tabs primitive skin across engines
--ds-tabs-list-bg.valueType: DS surface/colour/spacing/radius tokens; no raw literals
--ds-tabs-list-bg.subtreeRepaint: the one tab strip that owns the scope. RESIDUAL RISK: a tenant that sets chrome.tabs does not reach inside this scope. Declared, not hidden — this family is the strongest candidate for a DS-side per-scope override slot.
--ds-tabs-list-bg.rationale: Eight of these names the DS reads but never declares, which is the component-variable pattern in its purest form: the DS asks the context for a value. The feature tab strip is a navigational identity surface a vertical is expected to shape. Every value chains through --ds-surface-*, --ds-color-* and --ds-spacing-*, so a tenant palette change still flows through.

--ds-button-default-bg.owner: the Button primitive skin across engines (modern/rustic/classic) and the Button contract tokens
--ds-button-default-bg.slot: an explicit application control scope — a chip, suggestion, choice option, icon button or detail action bar
--ds-button-default-bg.valueType: DS surface/colour tokens and color-mix over them; no raw literals
--ds-button-default-bg.subtreeRepaint: buttons rendered inside the declared control scope. RESIDUAL RISK: a tenant that sets chrome.controls for these variants does not reach inside the scope. Declared, not hidden.
--ds-button-default-bg.rationale: The app re-uses the Button primitive to render chips and toggle options rather than rebuilding a native control — which is the outcome the DS wants — and a chip is not painted like a form button. Two entries (--ds-button-*-bg-hover assigned from --ds-button-*-hover-bg) are pure bridges over a DS naming split and propagate the tenant value verbatim.

--ds-button-secondary-border-hover.rationale: The app re-uses the Button primitive to render chips and toggle options rather than rebuilding a native control — which is the outcome the DS wants — and a chip is not painted like a form button. --ds-table-bg.slot: the composition scope where a table is nested inside a card surface
--ds-table-bg.valueType: the keyword `inherit`, or a var() read of the sibling channel
--ds-table-bg.fallback: the tenant-compiled table and card chrome
--ds-table-bg.subtreeRepaint: the table/card pair inside the composition scope. No value is invented: each assignment either inherits or reads the sibling primitive channel.
--ds-table-bg.rationale: Composing two DS primitives into one visual object requires telling the inner one to stop painting its own frame. Every assignment here is `inherit` or a direct read of the tenant channel it bridges, so the tenant value reaches the scope unchanged — this family overrides nothing.

--ds-workspace-shell-overlay.subtreeRepaint: the decorative overlay layer of the one frame that owns the scope.
--ds-workspace-shell-overlay.rationale: A detail frame suppresses the workspace overlay so the record content is the only figure on the page. Suppression is a layout decision the frame variant exists to express.
